newsitem.title: USA: Argentina sees Moody's upgrade within 2 yrs -Lagos.
newsitem.headline: Argentina sees Moody's upgrade within 2 yrs -Lagos.

text.p: Argentina can expect a ratings upgrade from Moody's Investors Service within about two years, Argentine central bank vice president Martin Lagos said on Wednesday.
"(Moody's) moves slowly. They will tell you we have a poor record from the 1980s which justifies rating Argentina below investment grade," Lagos told investors and reporters at a conference here.
"About two years from now we will be rated investment grade," he added.

Argentina currently has split long-term foreign currency ratings of B1 from Moody's and BB from Standard & Poor's. Last week, Moody's said its outlook on the country was "improving," meaning the agency may place Argentina's ratings on review within the next 12 to 18 months.
But Lagos said Moody's would likely wait for political developments such as the next midterm elections and the 1999 presidential elections before raising the country's ratings.
The central banker was more sanguine about his country's chances with other rating agencies, however.
"Maybe the other agencies will move faster than Moody's," he said.
In his presentation, Lagos underscored the central bank's positive economic growth forecast.
"With domestic investment at the current level, the economy can sustain a growth rate of about 6.0 percent a year," he said.
While solid economic expansion should help ease unemployment concerns, the jobless rate will probably decline gradually, Lagos said.
He projected the unemployment rate would read between 15.5 percent and 16.0 percent for May, compared with about 17.5 percent in the last reading, in October.

Asked whether the government would consider releasing economic indicators on a more-timely and -frequent basis, the central bank official said plans were underway to release jobless statistics four times a year rather than twice.
